entries.originalText: Be thou watchful and diligent in God’s service, and bethink thee often why thou hast renounced the world.
entries.modernizedText: Be watchful and diligent in God’s service, and often consider why you have renounced the world.

entries.originalText: Was it not that thou mightest live to God and become a spiritual man?
entries.modernizedText: Was it not so that you might live to God and become a spiritual person?

entries.originalText: Be zealous, therefore, for thy spiritual profit, for thou shalt receive shortly the reward of thy labours, and neither fear nor sorrow shall come any more into thy borders.
entries.modernizedText: Be zealous, therefore, for your spiritual benefit, for you will shortly receive the reward of your labors, and neither fear nor sorrow will come into your borders anymore.

entries.originalText: Now shalt thou labour a little, and thou shalt find great rest, yea everlasting joy.
entries.modernizedText: Now you will labor a little, and you will find great rest, indeed everlasting joy.

entries.originalText: If thou shalt remain faithful and zealous in labour, doubt not that God shall be faithful and bountiful in rewarding thee.
entries.modernizedText: If you remain faithful and zealous in labor, do not doubt that God will be faithful and generous in rewarding you.

entries.originalText: It is thy duty to have a good hope that thou wilt attain the victory, but thou must not fall into security lest thou become slothful or lifted up.
entries.modernizedText: It is your duty to have a good hope that you will attain victory, but you must not fall into a sense of security, lest you become slothful or lifted up.

entries.originalText: A certain man being in anxiety of mind, continually tossed about between hope and fear, and being on a certain day overwhelmed with grief, cast himself down in prayer before the altar in a church, and meditated within himself, saying, “Oh! if I but knew that I should still persevere,” and presently heard within him a voice from God, “And if thou didst know it, what wouldst thou do?
entries.modernizedText: A certain person, anxious in mind and continually tossed about between hope and fear, was one day overwhelmed with grief. He cast himself down in prayer before the altar in a church and meditated within himself, saying, “Oh, if only I knew that I would still persevere,” and soon heard within him a voice from God: “And if you knew it, what would you do?

entries.originalText: Do now what thou wouldst do then, and thou shalt be very secure.”
entries.modernizedText: Do now what you would do then, and you will be very secure.”

entries.originalText: And straightway being comforted and strengthened, he committed himself to the will of God and the perturbation of spirit ceased, neither had he a mind any more to search curiously to know what should befall him hereafter, but studied rather to inquire what was the good and acceptable will of God, for the beginning and perfecting of every good work.
entries.modernizedText: Immediately comforted and strengthened, he committed himself to the will of God, and the turmoil of spirit ceased. He no longer had a mind to search curiously to know what would befall him hereafter, but sought instead to inquire what was the good and acceptable will of God for beginning and perfecting every good work.

entries.originalText: Hope in the Lord and be doing good, saith the Prophet; dwell in the land and thou shalt be fed(1) with its riches.
entries.modernizedText: Hope in the Lord and be doing good, says the Prophet; dwell in the land and you will be fed(1) with its riches.

entries.originalText: One thing there is which holdeth back many from progress and fervent amendment, even the dread of difficulty, or the labour of the conflict.
entries.modernizedText: There is one thing that holds many back from progress and fervent amendment: dread of difficulty or of the labor of the struggle.

entries.originalText: Nevertheless they advance above all others in virtue who strive manfully to conquer those things which are most grievous and contrary to them, for there a man profiteth most and meriteth greater grace where he most overcometh himself and mortifieth himself in spirit.
entries.modernizedText: Nevertheless, those advance above all others in virtue who strive courageously to conquer the things most grievous and contrary to them, for a person benefits most and merits greater grace where he most overcomes himself and mortifies himself in spirit.

entries.originalText: But all men have not the same passions to conquer and to mortify, yet he who is diligent shall attain more profit, although he have stronger passions, than another who is more temperate of disposition, but is withal less fervent in the pursuit of virtue.
entries.modernizedText: But not all have the same passions to conquer and mortify; yet the diligent person will gain more benefit, although he has stronger passions, than another who is more temperate in disposition but less fervent in the pursuit of virtue.

entries.originalText: Two things specially avail unto improvement in holiness, namely firmness to withdraw ourselves from the sin to which by nature we are most inclined, and earnest zeal for that good in which we are most lacking.
entries.modernizedText: Two things especially help improvement in holiness: firmness in withdrawing from the sin to which we are by nature most inclined, and earnest zeal for the good in which we are most lacking.

entries.originalText: And strive also very earnestly to guard against and subdue those faults which displease thee most frequently in others.
entries.modernizedText: And strive very earnestly to guard against and subdue those faults that most frequently displease you in others.

entries.originalText: Gather some profit to thy soul wherever thou art, and wherever thou seest or hearest good examples, stir thyself to follow them, but where thou seest anything which is blameworthy, take heed that thou do not the same; or if at any time thou hast done it, strive quickly to amend thyself.
entries.modernizedText: Gather some benefit for your soul wherever you are, and wherever you see or hear good examples, stir yourself to follow them. But where you see anything blameworthy, take care not to do the same; or if you have ever done it, strive quickly to amend yourself.

entries.originalText: As thine eye observeth others, so again are the eyes of others upon thee.
entries.modernizedText: As your eye observes others, so the eyes of others are upon you.

entries.originalText: How sweet and pleasant is it to see zealous and godly brethren temperate and of good discipline; and how sad is it and grievous to see them walking disorderly, not practising the duties to which they are called.
entries.modernizedText: How sweet and pleasant it is to see zealous and godly brothers who are temperate and well disciplined; and how sad and grievous to see them walking disorderly, not practicing the duties to which they are called.

entries.originalText: How hurtful a thing it is to neglect the purpose of their calling, and turn their inclinations to things which are none of their business.
entries.modernizedText: How harmful it is to neglect the purpose of their calling and turn their inclinations to things that are none of their business.

entries.originalText: Be mindful of the duties which thou hast undertaken, and set always before thee the remembrance of the Crucified.
entries.modernizedText: Remember the duties you have undertaken, and always set before you the remembrance of the Crucified.

entries.originalText: Truly oughtest thou to be ashamed as thou lookest upon the life of Jesus Christ, because thou hast not yet endeavoured to conform thyself more unto Him, though thou hast been a long time in the way of God.
entries.modernizedText: Truly you ought to be ashamed as you look upon the life of Jesus Christ, because you have not yet endeavored to conform yourself more to Him, though you have long been in the way of God.

entries.originalText: A religious man who exercises himself seriously and devoutly in the most holy life and passion of our Lord shall find there abundantly all things that are profitable and necessary for him, neither is there need that he shall seek anything better beyond Jesus.
entries.modernizedText: A religious person who seriously and devoutly exercises himself in the most holy life and passion of our Lord will find there in abundance all things profitable and necessary for him, nor does he need to seek anything better beyond Jesus.

entries.originalText: Oh! if Jesus crucified would come into our hearts, how quickly, and completely should we have learned all that we need to know!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, if Jesus crucified would come into our hearts, how quickly and completely we would have learned all we need to know!

entries.originalText: He who is earnest receiveth and beareth well all things that are laid upon him.
entries.modernizedText: The earnest person receives and bears well all things laid upon him.

entries.originalText: He who is careless and lukewarm hath trouble upon trouble, and suffereth anguish upon every side, because he is without inward consolation, and is forbidden to seek that which is outward.
entries.modernizedText: The careless and lukewarm person has trouble upon trouble and suffers anguish on every side, because he is without inward consolation and is forbidden to seek outward consolation.

entries.originalText: He who is living without discipline is exposed to grievous ruin.
entries.modernizedText: The person living without discipline is exposed to grievous ruin.

entries.originalText: He who seeketh easier and lighter discipline shall always be in distress, because one thing or another will give him displeasure.
entries.modernizedText: The person who seeks easier and lighter discipline will always be in distress, because one thing or another will displease him.

entries.originalText: O! if no other duty lay upon us but to praise the Lord our God with our whole heart and voice!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, if no other duty lay upon us but to praise the Lord our God with our whole heart and voice!

entries.originalText: Oh! if thou never hadst need to eat or drink, or sleep, but wert always able to praise God, and to give thyself to spiritual exercises alone; then shouldst thou be far happier than now, when for so many necessities thou must serve the flesh.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, if you never needed to eat or drink or sleep, but were always able to praise God and give yourself to spiritual exercises alone, then you would be far happier than now, when you must serve the flesh for so many necessities.

entries.originalText: O! that these necessities were not, but only the spiritual refreshments of the soul, which alas we taste too seldom.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, that these necessities did not exist, but only the spiritual refreshments of the soul, which alas we taste too seldom.

entries.originalText: When a man hath come to this, that he seeketh comfort from no created thing, then doth he perfectly begin to enjoy God, then also will he be well contented with whatsoever shall happen unto him.
entries.modernizedText: When a person has come to seek comfort from no created thing, then he begins perfectly to enjoy God; then also he will be well content with whatever happens to him.

entries.originalText: Then will he neither rejoice for much nor be sorrowful for little, but he committeth himself altogether and with full trust unto God, who is all in all to him, to whom nothing perisheth nor dieth, but all things live to Him and obey His every word without delay.
entries.modernizedText: Then he will neither rejoice over much nor be sorrowful over little, but commits himself altogether and with full trust to God, who is all in all to him, to whom nothing perishes or dies, but all things live to Him and obey His every word without delay.

entries.originalText: Remember always thine end, and how the time which is lost returneth not.
entries.modernizedText: Always remember your end and how time that is lost does not return.

entries.originalText: Without care and diligence thou shalt never get virtue.
entries.modernizedText: Without care and diligence you will never gain virtue.

entries.originalText: If thou beginnest to grow cold, it shall begin to go ill with thee, but if thou givest thyself unto zeal thou shalt find much peace, and shalt find thy labour the lighter because of the grace of God and the love of virtue.
entries.modernizedText: If you begin to grow cold, things will begin to go badly for you; but if you give yourself to zeal, you will find much peace and find your labor lighter because of the grace of God and the love of virtue.

entries.originalText: A zealous and diligent man is ready for all things.
entries.modernizedText: A zealous and diligent person is ready for all things.

entries.originalText: It is greater labour to resist sins and passions than to toil in bodily labours.
entries.modernizedText: It is greater labor to resist sins and passions than to toil in bodily labor.

entries.originalText: He who shunneth not small faults falleth little by little into greater.
entries.modernizedText: The person who does not shun small faults falls little by little into greater ones.

entries.originalText: At eventide thou shalt always be glad if thou spend the day profitably.
entries.modernizedText: In the evening you will always be glad if you spend the day profitably.

entries.originalText: Watch over thyself, stir thyself up, admonish thyself, and howsoever it be with others, neglect not thyself.
entries.modernizedText: Watch over yourself, stir yourself up, admonish yourself, and however it may be with others, do not neglect yourself.

entries.originalText: The more violence thou dost unto thyself, the more thou shall profit.
entries.modernizedText: The more violence you do to yourself, the more you will benefit.

entries.originalText: Amen.
entries.modernizedText: Amen.
